tools.name: shell_command
tools.label: Shell Command
tools.description: Run a shell command inside the configured workspace. Use this for filesystem inspection, CLI workflows, and scripted operations. Git is allowed, but do not run commands that discard uncommitted work, such as git checkout --, git restore, git reset --hard, or git clean, unless the user explicitly asks to restore, reset, discard, or clean those changes. When repairing generated file corruption, preserve unrelated user edits and use targeted edits instead of restoring whole files. Do not run broad recursive scans from drive or system roots unless the user explicitly asks and the path and depth are narrowed.

timeoutMs.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds. Omit to use the configured default.

tools.name: invoke_model
tools.label: Invoke Model
tools.description: Call the default model or a specialist model profile. Route multimodal work through capability tags such as vision, image_generation, image_editing, speech_to_text, and text_to_speech.

profile.description: Optional profile id or name, or default

capability.description: Optional capability: orchestration, chat, vision, image_generation, image_editing, speech_to_text, text_to_speech, or embedding

prompt.description: Text prompt or edit instruction. Required for normal chat, image analysis questions, image generation, and image editing.

system.description: Optional system instruction for text-model calls

temperature.description: Optional temperature override for text-model calls

maxTokens.description: Optional max output tokens for text or vision responses

images.description: Optional image upload paths, URLs, or data URLs for capability=vision or capability=image_editing

audio.description: Optional audio upload path, URL, or data URL for capability=speech_to_text

detail.description: Optional image detail for vision calls: auto, low, high, or original

outputFormat.description: Optional output format such as png, jpeg, or webp

inputFidelity.description: Optional input fidelity for image editing: low or high

instructions.description: Optional speaking style instructions for text-to-speech

tools.name: create_scheduled_task
tools.label: Create Scheduled Task
tools.description: Create a scheduled task that appears in the Tasks panel and runs through Nexo's built-in scheduler. Use this when the user wants a reminder, recurring prompt, delayed follow-up, or an automated future run. Provide either cron, runAt, or delayMinutes. The task prompt is what the scheduled run will send into the agent.

name.description: Optional task name shown in the Tasks panel.

prompt.description: Required prompt content the task will send when it runs.

cron.description: Optional 5-field cron expression: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week.

runAt.description: Optional ISO 8601 datetime for a one-time future run.

delayMinutes.description: Optional delay in minutes from now for a one-time future run.

enabled.description: Optional enabled flag. Defaults to true.

runOnce.description: Optional one-time run flag. Defaults to true when runAt or delayMinutes is used without cron.

tools.name: recall_memory
tools.label: Recall Memory
tools.description: Search persistent daily, dream, or script memory stored in SQLite with embedding-backed recall when available.

kinds.description: Optional persistent memory kinds to search

tools.name: store_script_memory
tools.label: Store Script Memory
tools.description: Create or update a keyed script memory in SQLite for deterministic reusable workflows. Use this after turning a repeated user workflow into a stable script, command, runbook, captured browser request sample, or replay template that should be recalled across sessions.

key.description: Stable unique key for the workflow, such as workflow:release-build or project:nexo-agent:script-memory.

content.description: Complete reusable script memory content, including purpose, triggers, inputs, stable steps, command, outputs, and verification.

scope.description: Optional scope such as project, user, or team.

metadata.description: Optional structured metadata such as triggers, command, scriptPath, version, and verification commands.

dayKey.description: Optional YYYYMMDD day key. Omit to use today.

tools.name: browser_action
tools.label: Browser Action
tools.description: Operate the shared Electron browser session for conversational web browsing and web app control. Use only when the task explicitly involves navigating a website, checking a page, or interacting with a web app in the current conversation. Do not present it as a standalone feature, and do not use it for general HTTP requests, web search, file access, or credentialless automation. Each browser_action call performs exactly one browser operation and returns the updated page state; for multi-step workflows, call one action, inspect the returned state, then decide the next action. Standard control resolution is AX tree plus stable refs with stale re-resolution. For explicit BrowserView programming, raw CDP control, request capture, runtime debugging, reusable page instrumentation, or when the user explicitly asks for raw browser-runtime control, use action=script to run Electron-side service JavaScript with direct access to browserView, webContents, debugger/CDP, browserManager, scriptCache, and Node/Electron runtime objects. For request capture tasks such as listening to the user's form submission and replaying it later, action=script may write its own host/runtime script, including page instrumentation through webContents/CDP when needed. Return compact structured logs with method, URL, headers, body, status, and response snippets; short-lived capture samples are automatically stored in the action=script scriptCache when returned in a capture-like shape, and scripts can call scriptCache.set/get/getEntry/list/delete/clear/capture/consume/consumeEntry/replay directly. Use scriptCache for temporary request samples; when a sample has served its one-time purpose, consume/delete it or call replay with deleteAfter/deleteOnSuccess so temporary captures do not linger. Large tool outputs are bounded before they enter model context, so action=script should return concise summaries plus scriptCache keys or raw-output references instead of complete history/log/body arrays whenever possible. Promote only stable reusable scripts, runbooks, or replay templates to store_script_memory so future sessions can recall them with recall_memory. Do not use shell commands, PowerShell, or OS-level mouse/keyboard automation to operate ordinary browser UI controls. When visual state matters or the user asks to see the current page, call action=screenshot so the runtime can attach the screenshot to the assistant response. Before typing sensitive data or submitting forms, confirm the user intends that action.

script.description: Electron-side service JavaScript body for action=script. The script runs in an async function and can directly use browserView, webContents, debugger/CDP, browserManager, scriptCache, require, Buffer, process, and Electron runtime objects. Use it for explicit raw browser-runtime/CDP tasks, request capture, runtime debugging, or reusable page instrumentation. For capture scripts, return compact structured logs; capture-like return values are automatically stored in scriptCache, and scripts can directly call scriptCache.set/get/getEntry/list/delete/clear/capture/consume/consumeEntry/replay. Use consume/consumeEntry for one-time reads, or replay(key,{deleteAfter:true}) / replay(key,{deleteOnSuccess:true}) when the cached request should be removed after reuse. Avoid returning complete history/log/body arrays as normal tool output; large returns are bounded and moved to raw-output references. Use store_script_memory only when promoting a stable reusable script or replay template across sessions.

args.description: Optional positional arguments exposed to action=script as args.

scriptCacheKey.description: Optional key for action=script automatic scriptCache storage. When provided, the script return value is cached under this key even if it is not recognized as a capture log.

scriptCacheTtlMs.description: Optional TTL in milliseconds for action=script automatic cache storage and scriptCache writes that omit ttlMs. Defaults to 30 minutes and is capped by the browser runtime.

target.description: Target descriptor for click, type, resolve, wheel, hover, or drag. Prefer an object such as {"ref":"e1"}, {"query":"visible button label"}, or {"bounds":{...}}. A bare stable ref string like "e1" is also accepted for compatibility. If a snapshot or selected element provides bounds, prefer target.bounds over hand-written target.x/target.y so the runtime clicks the element center.

x.description: Viewport x coordinate for direct coordinate targets. Use only when no element bounds are available.

y.description: Viewport y coordinate for direct coordinate targets. Use only when no element bounds are available.

bounds.description: Element bounds from snapshot or selected-element output. For coordinate clicks, the runtime clicks the center or relativePosition within these bounds.

ref.description: Compatibility shortcut for target.ref; prefer putting this under target.

query.description: Compatibility shortcut for target.query; prefer putting this under target.

role.description: Compatibility shortcut for target.role; prefer putting this under target.

selector.description: Compatibility shortcut for target.selector; prefer putting this under target.

xpath.description: Compatibility shortcut for target.xpath; prefer putting this under target.

deltaX.description: Horizontal pixel delta for action=drag, or wheel delta override for action=wheel.

deltaY.description: Vertical pixel delta for action=drag, or wheel delta override for action=wheel.

timeoutMs.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds for action=script.

minConfidence.description: Minimum resolver confidence for query-based click/type.
